Prevention: Rotate with non- solanaceous crops such as maize, beans and peas for at least two seasons.
Destroy infected crop debris after harvesting.
Keep field weed free to reduce inoculum pressure.
Maintain optimal soil fertility to increase crop vigour.
Observe spacing of 70cm x 30cm to optimize aeration.
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: tomato, eggplant, pepper, black nightshade.
Brown spots with concentric rings on leaves appearing first on older leaves and progressing upwards.
Slightly sunken, circular or irregular surface lesions on tubers that are darker than adjacent healthy tissue.
Tubers with internal brown to black corky rot.
Take action when 5% of plants are affected in 100 plants.
Direct Control: Uproot severely infected plants and burn.
Gold at the rate of 250 g per 20
Restrictions: Wear protective clothing when handling pesticides

Start spraying shortly after transplanting when plants are about 15 cm high before symptoms appear
Spray every 7 to 10 days (more applications during dampy weather and less during dry weather).
